headline: Apple's iPhone Duo goes on sale, a poisoned LiteLLM release steals AI keys, Saudi Arabia downs another missile over Riyadh, and Delhi Police let Diljit Dosanjh sing after all
standfirst: Quad9 and eMudhra still lead Hacker News, but the day's new tech stories are Apple's first foldable, sold out into January, and a credential-stealing LiteLLM build that ran on any Python start-up. Abroad, Saudi air defences intercepted a Houthi missile over Riyadh before dawn while Israel prepares to seal the West Bank. In India, police reversed their concert refusal within two days, Jio's record IPO closed with the final count still pending, and the Sensex fell a fourth day.
notes: Third Phoenix run of 23 October, at 11:07 UTC (16:37 IST), from a session without a browser tool, so the owner's X feed was not read. Tech trend coverage comes from Hacker News (front-page maximum 1,236 points) and a web search.

Ground News: the home page showed only its Daily Briefing card (IRGC says 7 vessels hit near Hormuz, 8 stories, 736 articles) before truncating; /interest/world was empty again; /interest/india listed the iPhone Duo (119 sources), Goyal on CBAM (15) and the Diljit permission (8) as its top three and the Tusk Bengaluru forum as a Blindspot.

New in this edition: the iPhone Duo launch, the LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply-chain compromise, Warp Sciences, the Diljit Dosanjh reversal, and Friday's Saudi interceptions. Cards carried from earlier editions keep their published paragraphs with refreshed heat lines and scores.

Corrections to the 10:17 UTC edition, which stays as published: the Diljit Dosanjh concert has been granted permission (that edition said the refusal stood), and its headline figure of over 12 times for the Jio IPO rests on one broker page; the only NSE-sourced figure found is 8.22 times at 1:26 pm.
Checked and not used: a School Assembly headline that India beat New Zealand in a first T20I at Christchurch could not be found in any match report.

sections.blurb: Hacker News front page, security press, AI and market roundups. The X feed was not reachable this run.

stories.title: Quad9 will stop serving France on 24 November after a court orders it to block domains for beIN
stories.summary: The Swiss nonprofit DNS resolver says a Paris court ruling of 21 October leaves it unable to comply without either blocking globally or identifying users by country, so it is withdrawing from France entirely.
stories.heat: HN 1,236 pts · 415 comments · top of the front page all day, 1.0x the day's maximum
detail: Quad9 published a post titled Farewell, France on 22 October 2026 announcing that it will withdraw its free recursive DNS service (9.9.9.9 and 149.112.112.112, plus the IPv6 addresses 2620:fe::fe and 2620:fe::9) from France on Tuesday 24 November 2026. The post is signed by the Quad9 team, a Swiss foundation.

The trigger is a French court decision of 21 October in a case brought by beIN, the Qatari broadcaster with French offices, ordering Quad9 to block a set of domains for users in France. The daily penalty for non-compliance was reduced from EUR 580,000 to EUR 1,000, but Quad9 says the obligation itself is the problem: it does not log or geolocate users, so the only ways to comply are to block the domains for everyone worldwide or to start identifying which users are French.

Quad9 says an appeal is pending and that roughly 20 similar cases are open against it, so it expects more of the same. It frames the withdrawal as the least bad option for its users elsewhere, who would otherwise inherit French blocking orders.

French ISPs, mobile operators, schools and public networks that point at Quad9 for its malware blocking lose that resolver at the end of November and will need to pick another. The Hacker News thread, the largest of the day, argues over whether rights-holder DNS injunctions can work at all against resolvers that hold no user data.

stories.title: eMudhra abandons the global TLS certificate business after eight intermediate CA keys turned out to be guessable
stories.summary: The Bengaluru-listed certificate authority says the business was about 1 percent of revenue and the social-media scrutiny was out of proportion. Chrome distrusts its emSign ECC root on 27 October.
stories.heat: HN 1,068 pts · 691 comments, the most-discussed thread of the day · The Hacker News, Business Standard, Analytics India Magazine
detail: eMudhra's press release of 22 October 2026 (BSE 543533, NSE EMUDHRA) says the board has decided to voluntarily withdraw from the global SSL/TLS certificate business. Chairman V. Srinivasan says the affected certificate authorities were revoked within 14 hours of discovery, no end-entity certificates had been issued from them and no data was breached. The release says TLS was about 1 percent of global revenue and that attention on social media drew scrutiny out of proportion to the business's place in the company.

The incident behind the exit, as reported by The Hacker News on 22 October: a researcher reported on 17 October that the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CAs were recoverable because the key-generation process in April 2025 produced keys with far too little entropy. Chrome and Firefox blocked six TLS intermediates within hours. Mozilla decided on 20 October to distrust the emSign ECC Root CA G3 in Firefox, and Chrome's distrust of the same root takes effect on the morning of 27 October Pacific time.

Chrome counted about 30,800 unexpired certificates under that root as of 21 October, 99.9 percent of them issued through InCommon, the US research-and-education federation; Cornell alone reports more than 300. Those operators have until 27 October to replace them. Mozilla is not yet removing eMudhra's G1 RSA roots, which keep serving during the transition, and eMudhra says it will give affected customers free replacement certificates from unnamed partners.

eMudhra's other products (digital signature certificates, eSign, PKI and identity) are unaffected, and no exit date for the TLS business is given. As of 13:31 UTC on 22 October the company had not publicly answered the questions Chrome's root programme put to it, which is a large part of why the Hacker News thread runs to 671 comments.

sources.name: The Hacker News: weak CA keys and browser distrust

stories.title: Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, goes on sale with deliveries already slipping to late January
stories.summary: Reuters says sales began on Friday 23 October with stock limited in most markets and online-only pickup in China, India, Japan, France and Hong Kong. Reviews praise the hinge and fault the camera.
stories.heat: Ground News India top item: 119 sources, 49 percent centre · Reuters copy in Asharq Al-Awsat, The Standard, BusinessWorld, Euronext, Business Recorder · launch day
detail: Apple's first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, went on sale on Friday 23 October 2026, Reuters reported in a story carried by Asharq Al-Awsat, BusinessWorld, Business Recorder and Euronext. Within minutes of pre-orders opening, Apple's estimated delivery dates had slipped to late January, and Apple limited pre-orders to two handsets per customer.

Apple said walk-in availability would vary, with limited stock in the US, Australia, Canada, Mexico and much of Britain and Europe; in China, France, Hong Kong, India and Japan, units are available only to customers who ordered online. Reported prices include HK$17,499 (about 2,232 US dollars) for 256 GB in Hong Kong and A$3,899 (about 2,734 US dollars) for 512 GB in Australia.

Early reviews praised the design and the sturdy, barely visible hinge, but flagged the absence of a telephoto lens and third-party apps not yet reworked for the new display size. Reuters frames the launch as a test of whether Apple can revive the small foldables market. Ground News lists the story at 119 sources, the largest count on its India page today, which is why it leads there.

stories.title: PHP2Shell: two unauthenticated RCEs in PHP core patched a day early after the embargo broke on Hacker News
stories.summary: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 9.2) are fixed in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Cloudflare and watchTowr report exploitation attempts; the person who leaked the timing has apologised on HN.
stories.heat: Tell HN 574 pts · 221 comments · The Hacker News, iTnews, watchTowr, Black Kite · exploitation attempts reported since 21 October
detail: The PHP project released fixed versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 on 21 October 2026 at about 14:00 UTC for two remote code execution flaws in PHP core, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both rated CVSS v4.0 9.2 by PHP. Both allow unauthenticated code execution against any PHP install that serves web traffic; mod_php deployments carry the highest risk. Source backports exist for the unsupported 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 branches, and nothing is coming for PHP 5 or 7.0 to 7.3. The flaws were found by Wiz Research, Calif and OpenAI Codex Security and are being called PHP2Shell.

The disclosure was due later in the week. On 20 October a Hacker News user posted that the flaws existed and would be disclosed on 22 October; the PHP team responded by moving the release up a day. That user, petecooper, then posted Tell HN: I unknowingly broke the PHP RCE embargo, saying a contact had told him there was no embargo, that he compiles PHP from source and wanted to warn others, and that he takes full responsibility. The thread had 514 points and 207 comments when read; most replies argued he could not break an embargo he was never told about, while cperciva pointed out that embargo participants are responsible for who they share with and tptacek called the situation a five-alarm fire given working proofs of concept circulating privately.

Exploitation status is moving. Black Kite says Cloudflare first saw attack traffic at 07:43 UTC on 21 October, before the patch. watchTowr reported no exploitation at 11:26 UTC that day, then active exploitation attempts at 14:19 UTC. Neither CVE was in CISA's KEV catalogue at the time of those reports and no confirmed break-in has been published. Configuration workarounds circulating online are not complete fixes.
If you run PHP anywhere that faces the internet, upgrade to the fixed versions now. The leaked claim of a CVSS 10.0 score conflicts with PHP's official 9.2.

stories.title: Meta falls 7 percent and drags the Nasdaq down more than 2 percent as AI capex outruns cash flow
stories.summary: Meta beat on revenue but reported negative free cash flow and lifted 2026 capex guidance to 135 to 145 billion dollars. Chip stocks fell hardest; the semiconductor index dropped over 6 percent by one count.
stories.heat: Every market desk led with it (Reuters, Yahoo Finance, Kiplinger, Schwab) · Asia opened lower on it Friday · peaked at Thursday's close
detail: On Thursday 22 October 2026 Meta Platforms closed at about 648.85 dollars, down 6.98 percent, the day after its third-quarter report. Revenue beat expectations but earnings per share of 3.83 dollars missed, and quarterly free cash flow turned negative at minus 2.1 billion dollars as 34.9 billion dollars of capital spending exceeded 32.8 billion dollars of operating cash flow. Meta narrowed its 2026 capex guidance to 135 to 145 billion dollars from 130 to 145 billion and, separately, announced a 2-for-1 stock split and a non-voting Class C share class to keep funding AI.

The index moves differ by source: Kiplinger headlines a 694-point Nasdaq drop, another close puts the Nasdaq Composite down 590.94 points or 2.21 percent at 26,111.92, and a third says 2.6 percent. The S&P 500 fell between 1.2 and 1.4 percent. Nvidia fell about 4.4 percent and the SMH semiconductor ETF about 3.4 percent; one report has the SOX index down over 6 percent and ties part of the drop to remarks by Nvidia's Jensen Huang about capital shortages, which no other outlet confirmed.

Reuters framed the day as Meta's report reigniting worries about the AI boom's capital spending and sending investors into Treasuries. ABC Australia's market blog put the year's combined AI spend by Microsoft, Oracle, Amazon, Meta and Alphabet at 804 billion US dollars. The same session saw Brent crude above 112 dollars after the Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia (see Geopolitics), SK Hynix put the US IPO of its Solidigm unit on hold, and Bitcoin fell 2.8 percent to about 81,600 dollars.

Update for this edition: AI Weekly's 23 October roundup puts the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down 6.7 percent on Thursday, which matches the larger of the chip-index figures above, and says a new Meta filing shows about 825 billion dollars in total future commitments, mostly AI compute and data centres, up from about 700 billion in July. India TV's market note says Japan's Nikkei fell 1.36 percent to 62,050 on Friday morning as the selling moved into Asia. The 825 billion figure rests on that one roundup and the filing itself was not read.

stories.title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 shipped a credential stealer on PyPI and Docker after attackers took three developers' GitHub credentials
stories.summary: Seven malicious wheels were live on PyPI for about 100 minutes on 21 October and the payload runs whenever Python starts, even without importing litellm. Safe version: 1.106.2. Rotate credentials if you installed 1.107.0.
stories.heat: LiteLLM incident report · Wiz, Datadog, Socket, Chainguard, StepSecurity, Mend, SafeDep all published · about 49,000 downloads per Wiz
detail: LiteLLM, the widely used Python library and proxy for calling many AI model APIs, says in its incident report that release v1.107.0 was compromised on 21 October 2026. Malicious wheels were on PyPI from roughly 11:39 to 13:23 UTC; the project counts seven wheels in total. The same payload was in the project's container images for that tag until they were pulled from GHCR (by 13:51 UTC) and Docker Hub (14:20 or 14:32 UTC, depending on the report). The v1.107.0 source tag on GitHub does not contain the malicious files.

The payload installs three files into site-packages, two of which run whenever any Python process starts on the host, even one that never imports litellm. StepSecurity and others describe a credential stealer aimed at cloud and AI keys plus an hourly remote code loader. Wiz cites ClickPy data for about 49,000 downloads.

LiteLLM says the attacker held GitHub CLI credentials belonging to three developers, used them to get past branch protection, and pointed the private release workflow at a lookalike repository, Berri-AI/litellm. Chainguard's headline calls it LiteLLM attacked again. The advice from every vendor is the same: remove 1.107.0, pin 1.106.2 or later clean releases, check lockfiles and build logs for the bad version, and rotate any credentials on affected machines. Customers on the private enterprise build are reported unaffected.

stories.title: WorldTUI: a 360M-parameter model trained to pretend to be a terminal
stories.summary: Simon Edwardsson fine-tuned a Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B derivative on 336,000 Docker shell sessions so that each keypress produces predicted screen rows, no real shell involved. He calls it not really useful, and HN loved it anyway.
stories.heat: HN 553 pts · 171 comments
detail: In a post dated 21 October 2026, Simon Edwardsson (a co-founder of V7) describes WorldTUI, a 360-million-parameter model distilled from Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B and quantised to int4 at 208 MB, which acts as a terminal with no shell behind it. Each keypress goes in and the model predicts which screen rows and cursor position change. It was trained on about 336,000 recorded episodes, roughly 2 billion tokens, captured from real Docker sessions, in about 75 GPU-hours on a single RTX 4090.

On the author's ShellBench it scores 80 of 106 against 52 and 60 for prompted baseline models, and it reads back files it was shown earlier 9 times out of 13 where the baselines manage 2 and 3. The browser demo runs at about 60 ms per keystroke on an M4 Mac and works best in Chrome. Weights are promised soon. The HN thread treats it as a neat world-model toy and a reminder of how far small models go with narrow training data.

stories.title: Docker is weird: a runtime author's tour of what a container actually is
stories.summary: A Code and Cake post argues a container is a restricted process built from about five kernel features, that runc needs a C shim because Go cannot fork, and that rootless networking has to be rebuilt in userspace.
stories.heat: HN 526 pts · 233 comments · still climbing
detail: The post, dated 22 October 2026 and written by someone building an early-stage container runtime, walks through the oddities that surprised them: images are just folders that runc chroots or pivot_roots into; runc carries a C module called nsenter and re-executes /proc/self/exe because Go has no fork; Docker normally runs as root, and the rootless mode has to reimplement networking entirely in userspace. There are no numbers; it is an explainer, and the HN thread is people adding their own favourite Docker oddities.

sources.name: Code and Cake: Docker is weird

stories.title: Local Wikipedia: Wikipedia articles for places within a half-hour walk of you
stories.summary: A small web app by Ed Jefferson that shows the geotagged Wikipedia articles nearest to you. HN liked it and asked for a distance setting and more languages.
stories.heat: HN 467 pts · 112 comments · the fastest climber on the front page since the last edition
detail: Local Wikipedia, at edjefferson.com/localwiki, takes the browser's location and lists the closest 25 geotagged Wikipedia articles within about 6 miles, or up to 500 if there are more. The location stays in the browser, and the site says it has no affiliation with Wikipedia.

The Hacker News thread (399 points and 103 comments when read) mostly praises the idea. The main requests are a configurable distance and other language editions, since English coverage is thin outside the US and Europe. Several commenters point out that Wikipedia's own Special:Nearby page and the Wikipedia mobile app already do something similar.

stories.title: Twelve AI models asked for their most controversial take on humans mostly gave the same one
stories.summary: ModelCompare ran 12 models three times each; 29 of 35 valid answers said humans prefer belonging and status to truth. Claude Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, GLM 5.3 and Mistral Large 4 were the exceptions.
stories.heat: HN 445 pts · 449 comments, the second-longest thread of the day
detail: ModelCompare's post of 22 October 2026 asked 12 text models, three runs each, for their most controversial opinion about humans. Of 35 valid answers (Grok 4.7 refused once), 29 landed on a version of the same idea: people value belonging or status more than truth. Seven of the 12 models gave that answer all three times. The exceptions were Claude Opus 5.5, which said humans are more decent than they believe, Claude Fable 5.1, GLM 5.3 and Mistral Large 4. The whole experiment cost 1.54 dollars across 60 calls.

The HN thread is mostly about whether the convergence shows shared training data, RLHF pushing models to the same safe-sounding provocation, or something true about people. The sample is tiny and the prompt was one sentence, so the post is a conversation starter rather than a result.

stories.title: A repo claims to boot the unmodified iOS 16.5 kernel and userspace on a POCO X5 Pro
stories.summary: hackios-xnu-kernel says XNU runs on a Snapdragon Android phone from a RAM-only fastboot boot, with lock screen, apps, Wi-Fi and camera working and cellular, Bluetooth and the App Store not. Two commits, self-reported screenshots.
stories.heat: HN 445 pts · 167 comments · two commits, self-reported screenshots
detail: The GitHub repository oosexgang/hackios-xnu-kernel claims that XNU build xnu-8796.121.2, the iOS 16.5 kernel, boots on a POCO X5 Pro 5G and under QEMU and runs the stock iOS 16.5 userspace, loaded into RAM over fastboot so nothing is flashed. The README lists lock screen, home screen, apps, Wi-Fi at 55 to 90 Mbit/s, sound, camera and GPU as working, and cellular, Bluetooth, charging, App Store and Apple ID sign-in as not. It says no Apple files are included and that the IPSW is fetched from Apple's CDN at build time.

The documentation is specific and the limitations are plausible, but the repository has two commits, the evidence is screenshots from the author, and nobody in the HN thread reports reproducing it. Treat it as an interesting claim until someone independent boots it.

stories.title: NVIDIA open-sources OpenShell, a kernel-enforced sandbox runtime for fleets of AI agents
stories.summary: Apache-2.0, 18,100 stars: agents run with kernel-level file, syscall and network policy, never see real credentials, and risky policy changes get flagged for human review. Telemetry is on by default.
stories.heat: HN 410 pts · 195 comments · 18.1k GitHub stars
detail: NVIDIA's OpenShell repository describes itself as the safe, private runtime for autonomous AI agents. Policies for file, syscall and network access are enforced at the kernel level; agents never hold real credentials, which are injected only at approved endpoints; and a formal-verification step flags risky policy changes for a human to approve. The project is Apache-2.0, on a 0.1.x release cadence, with 1,852 commits, 373 open issues and 192 open pull requests at read time.

It installs with a curl-to-shell script followed by openshell sandbox create, and needs Linux, Apple Silicon macOS or Windows under WSL 2 (experimental) plus Docker, Podman or host virtualisation. Telemetry is enabled by default and switched off with the OPENSHELL_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false environment variable, which drew a predictable share of the HN comments. It arrives the same week as two startups raising for the same niche: Rein (25 million dollars) and Asymptote Labs (5.5 million dollar seed), both pitching runtime security for agents.

stories.title: Anthropic: Claude wrote crash-freedom proofs for 239 fuzz targets across 123 OSS-Fuzz libraries
stories.summary: Working with Theorem, the Frontier Red Team had Claude prove at RISC-V assembly level that inputs under 64 MB cannot crash the targets, about 180 million lines of Rocq in all. The post is careful to say verified does not mean bug-free.
stories.heat: HN 354 pts · 209 comments
detail: Anthropic's research post of 22 October 2026, written with the verification company Theorem, reports that Claude produced machine-checked proofs that 239 fuzzing entry points in 123 OSS-Fuzz libraries cannot crash on any input under 64 MB. The proofs are at the level of RISC-V assembly and rest on stated assumptions: single-threaded static binaries built against musl, fixed memory, Linux. The combined proof corpus is about 180 million lines of Rocq, with a typical proof around 600,000 lines.

Along the way Claude found real bugs, including a rediscovery of CVE-2026-56132 in libexpat. On a set of 36 smaller tasks, Claude Opus 5.5 solved half while using about 40 percent fewer tokens than Opus 5. The authors stress that the proved property is narrow, that the model is RISC-V and musl rather than x86 and glibc, and that formally verified in this sense does not mean free of bugs. The Hacker News thread mostly debates how much the assumptions give away and whether proof volume at this scale is reviewable by humans at all.

stories.title: Ars Technica: Xbox wants 24 to 40 cents an hour to stream games you already own
stories.summary: The HN thread runs to 253 comments on the pricing of Xbox's cloud streaming for owned titles. The Ars page refused this run's reader, so the card rests on the headline and the thread.
stories.heat: HN 309 pts · 285 comments
detail: Ars Technica's gaming desk reports that Microsoft's Xbox cloud streaming for games a player already owns is priced at the equivalent of 24 to 40 cents per hour. The article could not be fetched for this edition (the site blocks automated readers), so the figures are taken from the headline alone. The Hacker News discussion at 253 comments is about whether metered streaming of owned games is a reasonable cost-recovery model or a new rent on purchases.

stories.title: Ask HN: if the models are so good, why doesn't OpenAI just start 100 companies?
stories.summary: A question thread on why AI labs sell tokens instead of building the applications themselves. The top answer: token sales to long-running agents are the only revenue that is provably working.
stories.heat: HN 180 pts · 179 comments, one comment per point
detail: The poster, ex-aws-dude, asks why OpenAI does not use its own models to start companies, noting that falling token prices may move the money to the application layer. The top reply argues that selling tokens to long-running agents is the only thing that is provably working for revenue, and that OpenAI needs that revenue because its borrowing costs are rising. Other replies say frontier models are not yet good enough to run a business alone, and that the sell-the-shovels logic of a gold rush applies. It sits next to the Meta spending selloff in the same day's news.

stories.title: Kevin Weil, OpenAI's former science chief, launches Warp Sciences with a 215 million dollar Series A for AI-run chemistry labs
stories.summary: Lightspeed led the round at an 865 million dollar post-money valuation. Warp wants a fully automated US lab whose chemists wear cameras and pressure-sensing gloves to generate training data.
stories.heat: Bloomberg exclusive, The Next Web, Ground News, Techmeme · announced 22 October
detail: Kevin Weil, who ran product and then science at OpenAI, announced Warp Sciences on X on Thursday 22 October 2026 with a 215 million dollar Series A led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, first reported by Bloomberg. IVP, Premji Invest and Lux Capital also took part, and the reported post-money valuation is 865 million dollars. The company aims to speed up a key chemistry step in drug development by bringing that work back to the US in a fully automated lab.

Its chemists will wear cameras and pressure-sensing gloves during experiments to produce data for training Warp's own models. The co-founders are Manohar Paluri, formerly a vice president at Meta's Superintelligence Labs, DJ Patil, the first US chief data scientist, and Solomon Reisberg, formerly of Terremoto Biosciences. In August Weil was reported to be raising 150 million dollars at a valuation of at least 750 million for the then-unnamed company.

stories.title: Also in AI: DeepSeek reported to raise about 15 billion dollars; Microsoft's diagnosis agent in Science; Reuters counts AI-linked job cuts
stories.summary: Three items from AI Weekly's 23 October roundup and a market search. None of the primary reports was read, so the card is unverified.
stories.heat: AI Weekly daily roundup, one market search · single-source items
detail: AI Weekly reports that DeepSeek raised about 15 billion dollars (roughly 100 billion yuan), with Tencent and CATL among the lead backers, two days after a US order to remove DeepSeek technology from federal agencies. The same page says a Science paper published on 22 October found Microsoft's MAI-DxO orchestrator correctly diagnosed 83 percent of complex New England Journal of Medicine cases against 36 percent for primary-care physicians working alone. A search found only the July 2025 preprint (85.5 percent against 20 percent for 21 physicians), so the Science version and its figures are not confirmed.

A market search also surfaced a Reuters count of about 102,800 announced job cuts at 31 companies since October 2025 that Reuters links to AI. Separately, a report that SpaceX is negotiating access to 80,000 US cell sites, which a market feed said knocked Verizon shares, could not be found in any other outlet and has no card.

stories.title: US orders non-emergency staff and families out of Saudi Arabia after Houthi strikes on airports and an Aramco field
stories.summary: The State Department's order of 21 to 22 October follows attacks on King Fahd airport in Dammam and a drone whose debris killed two workers at an Aramco oil field. Other Gulf missions are to send families home too.
stories.heat: Ground News lead yesterday (1,536 articles) · Bloomberg, Reuters, Al Jazeera, Arab News, Middle East Eye, The National · new interceptions overnight
detail: State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said on X that the department has ordered the departure of non-emergency US government employees and their family members from Saudi Arabia only, citing Houthi attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure that caused civilian casualties and severe travel disruption. Four US officials told reporters that US missions in other Gulf states would also order family members to leave. Stars and Stripes describes it as nonessential embassy personnel and families.

The attack with the clearest count is the one on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam: Reuters, carried in the Times of Israel liveblog of 22 October, reports one person killed and eight injured. Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry separately said debris from an intercepted drone killed two people, Nepali and Filipino nationals, at an Aramco-operated oil field in the south-east, with Pakistani and Indian nationals among the injured. The Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi defence and energy targets and on Dammam airport the same afternoon. An AFP-sourced report that Aramco told staff at its Dhahran headquarters to work from home after a missile damaged the building last week is single-sourced.

The Yemen front is widening the regional war that began with the US and Israeli campaign against Iran. Anadolu's 20 October briefing reports more than 53 people killed and over 200 injured in a Houthi attack on a security training centre in Shabwa province. Turkey will put a mandate before parliament to deploy military personnel to Saudi Arabia under the Mecca pact with Pakistan, and Egypt's parliament postponed to 26 October a vote on military support for the kingdom. Iran's foreign minister Araghchi said Tehran had received no response from Riyadh or the Houthis to its offer to mediate; the Houthis deny launching drones at Medina.

For India the practical effect is in the air: Air India, Air India Express, IndiGo and Akasa have suspended Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam flights until at least 24 October, Akasa until 27 October (see the India section). Brent crude traded near 112 to 113 dollars a barrel on Thursday.

Update for this edition: the Saudi-led coalition says air defences destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile fired at Riyadh shortly after 4 am on Friday 23 October, and two drones aimed at the south at about 1 am, according to spokesman Turki Al-Maliki (Arab News, Middle East Eye). Riyadh's civil defence issued an alert at about 5:14 am and lifted it minutes later; an alert in Najran was also lifted, and Anadolu reported no immediate casualties or damage. The National's live page counts at least 14 ballistic missiles and more than 60 armed drones fired at the kingdom in October. The Jerusalem Post reports, citing an Israeli defence official, that Israeli military intelligence is sharing capabilities with Saudi Arabia for its operations against the Houthis.

NewsNation: US orders diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia

stories.title: US and Israel have drawn up plans to strike Iran after the 3 November midterms; Trump says something will happen fairly soon
stories.summary: The New York Times, citing US officials, says energy, nuclear and missile sites are the targets and Trump has not approved. Iran's IRGC says seven vessels have hit mines or been struck near Hormuz; Trump calls the hits fake.
stories.heat: Ground News Daily Briefing lead today: IRGC says 7 vessels hit near Hormuz (8 stories, 736 articles) · NYT story carried by NPR, CNBC, Stars and Stripes · 28 attacks on Hormuz shipping this month
detail: The New York Times reported late on 21 October 2026, citing US officials, that the United States and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the US midterm elections on 3 November, with Iranian energy sites, nuclear facilities and missile and drone arsenals as possible targets. The plans followed Defense Secretary Hegseth's meeting with Netanyahu in Israel. Trump has not approved them and, per CNBC, has repeatedly vetoed a return to major combat this year. The Financial Times reported that an IDF offensive planned for 10 October was shelved over Trump's opposition, and the Times of Israel liveblog carried a report that the IDF chief sees no operational need to strike before the US election.

Trump said on 22 October that the US is not negotiating with Iran and that something, one way or another, will happen fairly soon. The same evening he said Iran is making up fake hits, mines and everything else to drive oil prices up before the midterms. Iran's president Pezeshkian says there will be no talks until Iran's demands are met, and parliament speaker Qalibaf has set seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Foreign minister Araghchi has said Tehran would give diplomacy another chance but warned further US military action would be a greater strategic failure.

At sea, the IRGC said on 22 October that four oil-carrying vessels had been hit and caught fire in the northern Gulf and three more collided with mines west of Hormuz, and warned that continued provocations would extend the conflict to US regional bases. None of the mine incidents is independently confirmed. The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre reported an unknown projectile striking a tanker near Bukha, Oman, on Wednesday. Noam Raydan of the Washington Institute counts at least 28 attacks on ships in the Hormuz region this month against 19 confirmed in March.

CBS reports the US is quietly reducing troop numbers at some Middle East bases; about 50,000 US personnel are deployed in the region. Israeli jets flew toward the Iranian border on Monday in what Israel called a training exercise. Brent was near 112 dollars on Thursday; the US struck Iranian mine-laying vessels in late August and declared the main shipping lane cleared the week before that.

stories.title: Israel orders the army to prepare a full West Bank closure and seals off Hebron after an attack wounds at least five
stories.summary: Soldiers killed two Palestinian attackers at a junction near Hebron on Friday 23 October. Netanyahu cancelled Likud events four days before Tuesday's election; Smotrich called for a campaign in the West Bank exactly like in Gaza.
stories.heat: ABC Australia, Al Jazeera, Jerusalem Post, Dawn, Türkiye Today · Israeli election on Tuesday 27 October
detail: Israeli soldiers shot and killed two Palestinian men who attacked near Hebron on Friday 23 October 2026, injuring at least five people, some critically, ABC News Australia reported at 7:18 pm Sydney time. Other reports place it at the Judea junction on Route 35, also known as the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint. The military said it prevented a terror attack against Israeli civilians.

Netanyahu's office said security forces were told to cordon off Hebron immediately and the military to prepare a full closure of the West Bank. Reports differ on how far the closure has gone: one outlet says entry and exit were to be blocked from Friday morning, others say only that the army is preparing it. Netanyahu, who faces an election on Tuesday, told Likud to cancel all political events on Friday morning.

Hamas called it an exceptional heroic operation and mourned the two dead men but did not claim it; ABC says there is no evidence the Palestinian Authority was connected. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for a comprehensive military campaign in the West Bank exactly like in Gaza, repeating a line he used on 27 September. Al Jazeera reports Israeli forces arrested 36 Palestinians in raids on Thursday and that attacks on olive harvesters have risen before the election; this follows the detention of American activists accompanying harvesters earlier in the week (see the Gaza card).

stories.title: Russia hits Kyiv with 21 ballistic missiles hours after agreeing in principle to resume three-way talks
stories.summary: Zelenskyy says the overnight strike on 22 October hit 12 regions and killed at least four. Moscow told Witkoff talks could start after 10 November; the October energy truce has collapsed on both sides.
stories.heat: AP, Reuters, PBS, CBS, Japan Times · talks pencilled for November
detail: Overnight into Thursday 22 October 2026 Russia launched a large missile and drone attack on Kyiv. Zelenskyy said at least 21 ballistic missiles struck the city, hitting railway stations and energy facilities, and that attacks across 12 regions killed at least four people; the interior minister's earlier count for Kyiv alone was one dead and 22 wounded. Russia's defence ministry said it intercepted more than 800 Ukrainian drones aimed at Moscow and other cities. A day earlier Ukrainian police reported four killed in Russian strikes on energy sites in four regions.

The strike came hours after Russia agreed in principle, following Steve Witkoff's meeting with Putin in St Petersburg on 20 October, to resume trilateral talks with the US and Ukraine, without fixing a date but suggesting after 10 November. Witkoff drew criticism for calling Putin a humanitarian; Rubio told Zelenskyy that Trump has not ordered anything to harm Ukraine; Zelenskyy insists on nothing about Ukraine without Ukraine. Russia released the detained US citizen Stephen Hubbard as a goodwill gesture before the meeting.

The energy ceasefire Trump announced on 11 October has effectively ended. Ukraine paused strikes on Russian energy targets for three days and resumed them, saying Russia never stopped; Russia has kept hitting Ukrainian energy sites including in Kharkiv. The Wall Street Journal reports Musk ordered Starlink service for Ukraine slowed, a single-source claim. Reuters says Russia's first diesel tanker to the US, carrying 40,000 tonnes, sails on Thursday.

Update for this edition: the Japan Times reports on 23 October (via search; the page refused the reader) that Putin confirmed Russia is ready to resume US-mediated talks next month, and that Ukraine sent hundreds of drones toward Moscow on Thursday while Russia hit Kyiv with ballistic missiles. Kremlin officials say a deal is theoretically possible but needs Ukraine's leaders to make necessary decisions. Zelenskyy said he would not accept any settlement drawn up by China, Russia and the US, and that any negotiated end to the war would need approval by Ukraine's parliament.

Paris police said on 21 October that curfews in two zones, around Place de la République and the Les Halles shopping district, had restored public peace overnight and would stay for as long as necessary; Lyon has curfews in parts of its centre.

Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said soldiers from the Sentinelle anti-terror operation will guard sensitive sites so police can concentrate on crowd control, and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu promised a massive police deployment for the protests called for Saturday 24 October. stories.title: Two days of US-hosted Lebanon-Israel military talks in Tampa end without a breakthrough as strikes on the south continue
stories.summary: Israel rejected Lebanon's demand for a third-party verification mechanism and says it will not withdraw until Hezbollah is disarmed nationwide. No further session is scheduled.
stories.heat: The New Arab, Shafaq, Times of Israel · strikes continue
detail: The New Arab's Rita El Jammal reports from Beirut on 22 October 2026 that two days of military-level talks between Lebanon and Israel at CENTCOM headquarters in Tampa, hosted by the United States, ended without agreement. Israel rejected Lebanon's demand for a third-party mechanism to verify compliance with the June framework agreement, and Lebanese military sources say no further session is scheduled. Defence Minister Israel Katz has said Israel will not leave southern Lebanon until Hezbollah is disarmed across the whole country.

On Thursday Israeli forces carried out demolitions in Tallouseh and Bani Hayyan and strikes hit Qantara and Kfar Tebnit; Shafaq reported heavy shelling of several southern towns with no casualty figures. Lebanese health officials counted 4,389 killed and 12,424 wounded since 2 March as of 12 October. President Joseph Aoun says Israel is violating the June deal; Israeli officials have spoken of a Gaza model for the south. In Lebanon's cabinet, a request is pending to refer the explosives seizures of 5 and 9 October to the Judicial Council.

A live tracker's cumulative Gaza toll stands at 74,498 dead and 175,616 injured since October 2023.

stories.title: Jio Platforms' Rs 30,213 crore IPO, India's largest ever, closes; NSE data had it 8.2 times covered by early afternoon
stories.summary: Upstox, citing NSE data, had the issue 8.22 times subscribed at 1:26 pm with institutions at 17.65 times. A broker page's 12.55 times at 3 pm is unconfirmed. Allotment 26 October, listing 28 October.
stories.heat: Reuters, Upstox (NSE data), HDFC Sky, every Indian business desk · bidding closed today · final figure not yet published
detail: Jio Platforms' initial public offering opened on 21 October 2026 and closes on Friday 23 October. The issue is Rs 30,213 crore, the largest in Indian history, a fresh issue of 27 crore shares at a price band of Rs 1,065 to 1,119 with a minimum lot of 12 shares, valuing the company at about Rs 10.3 lakh crore at the top of the band. Reuters puts the valuation at up to 108.3 billion dollars. Anchor investors including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, BlackRock and Fidelity bid for their reserved 854 million dollar quota with bids exceeding 25 billion dollars.

Reuters reports the offer was fully subscribed within two hours of opening on Wednesday and had crossed six times the shares on offer by Friday morning, with total demand above 14.5 billion dollars at the top price. FreeJobAlert's digest records 5.57 times coverage by the end of day two and bids of about Rs 1.25 lakh crore by Friday morning. The Analytics Insight live blog shows institutional demand at 13.35 to 14.67 times and non-institutional at 7.27 times during the morning; its figures are not fully consistent across entries. The grey market premium was about 22 percent, roughly Rs 246 on the top price, which is unofficial.

Proceeds go mainly to repaying up to Rs 27,500 crore of debt at Reliance Jio Infocomm. Jio, led by Akash Ambani, serves over 500 million mobile users and counts Meta and Google among existing investors. Reuters frames the listing as a test of appetite for large offers at a moment when AI-linked stocks are under scrutiny, and notes Reliance shares have returned about 900 percent since 2006 against 685 percent for the Nifty. Shares are expected to list on the BSE and NSE on 28 October. The RBI minutes (next card) credit IPO-related inflows with helping the rupee this week.

Allotment is scheduled for 26 October and listing on the BSE and NSE for 28 October.

Correction to the previous edition: its headline used HDFC Sky's figure of 12.55 times at 3 pm as if settled. The only NSE-sourced number found is Upstox's 8.22 times at 1:26 pm (QIB 17.65 times, non-institutional 11.47 times, retail 2.20 times), and the jump to 12.55 times in 90 minutes is unconfirmed. stories.title: Voter-roll fight, week three: Amit Shah attacks vote chori claims as the Election Commission reverses itself on searchable rolls
stories.summary: 130 million names came off the rolls in the Special Intensive Revision. The Hindu reports bulk deletions through auto-generated Form 7s with no SOP; Hindustan Times says the ECI dropped its promise of searchable rolls without adding safeguards.
stories.heat: NPR, Time, Al Jazeera, The Hindu, Hindustan Times, UNI · a running story, not a spike
detail: The Election Commission of India's Special Intensive Revision removed more than 130 million names from the electoral rolls: about 95 million (71 percent) as absent, shifted or other, 27 million as deceased and 10 million as duplicates, per the breakdown current to September 2026. Opposition parties led by Rahul Gandhi have held protests demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation; the Supreme Court has said the data does not indicate systemic disenfranchisement; in West Bengal 3.7 million of 3.8 million appeals were still pending.

This week's developments, as reported by The Hindu on 15 and 16 October: the ECI ordered an annual Special Summary Revision across 14 states and 3 union territories with a qualifying date of 1 January 2027, and state electoral officers were given no standard operating procedure for the auto-generated Form 7 deletion notices through which thousands of names in the absent-shifted-dead list were removed without the usual procedure. Hindustan Times reported on 18 October that thousands queued at Delhi SIR camps before a deadline and on 19 October that the ECI reversed its stand on providing searchable electoral rolls without adding safeguards. Indian Express reports Congress is now demanding a machine-readable voter list.

On Thursday 22 October, his birthday, Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurated 43 Delhi Jal Board projects worth Rs 8,941 crore for the Yamuna and used the occasion to attack Congress and AAP over their vote chori allegations, saying Congress would not return to power for 30 years. Separately, Naveen Patnaik demanded the release of two Cockroach Janta Party leaders held in judicial custody since a 13 October protest at Jantar Mantar, and Mamata Banerjee called the extension of their custody state-sponsored terrorism, an item 17 outlets carried.

Update for this edition: UNI's 23 October digest leads with Modi's escalating attack on Rahul Gandhi, and carries Congress accusing the government of silence on border face-offs with China. Polling for four Karnataka Legislative Council seats began at 8 am, and the Centre extended the deployment of 273 CAPF companies in Delhi to 31 October amid fears of flash protests (both from search summaries of the same digest; the text is partly paywalled).

stories.title: Delhi Police reverse themselves and allow Diljit Dosanjh's 30 October JLN Stadium concert after meetings with organisers
stories.summary: Two days after refusing on threat inputs, police granted permission once BookMyShow Live presented a security plan and accepted extra crowd and traffic conditions. Heavy vehicles are barred from BP Marg on show days.
stories.heat: ANI, Free Press Journal, Oneindia, The Hans India · Ground News India top item: 8 sources, 50 percent right · reversed within 48 hours
detail: Delhi Police have granted permission for Diljit Dosanjh's Aura India Tour concert at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on 30 October 2026, ANI reported on 23 October, reversing the refusal that DCP (South) Anant Mittal sent BookMyShow on 21 October citing threat inputs and festive-season security commitments. Police officials told Free Press Journal and Oneindia the decision followed several meetings with the organisers, who presented detailed security plans.

Police asked BookMyShow Live for additional safety, traffic and crowd-management measures, and the company said it assured full compliance; it also said permission had been temporarily withheld, never cancelled. A traffic advisory restricts heavy vehicles from the JLN Stadium red light along BP Marg from 4 pm to 11 pm on the show days. Opposition politicians had called the refusal political targeting of an artist who backed farmers and students; police cited only security and public order.
Correction to the previous edition: it said the refusal stood and treated a report of permission as unsupported. That report was early, not wrong. The earlier cards are left as published.

stories.title: Goyal in Berlin calls the EU's carbon border tax on steel an invitation to disaster; India-EU FTA still pencilled for end-2026
stories.summary: Speaking at the Berlin Global Dialogue on 22 October, the commerce minister said CBAM and a 50 percent steel duty would raise European living costs and invite retaliation. Mint says the FTA would give over 99 percent of Indian exports by value preferential access.
stories.heat: Ground News India top item: 15 sources, 67 percent right-leaning coverage · Economic Times, Mint, Fortune India
detail: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal, speaking at the Berlin Global Dialogue on Thursday 22 October 2026, said the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism on steel is inviting disaster. He argued that a 50 percent import duty on steel and a growing set of rules would raise living costs in Europe, weaken its competitiveness and invite retaliatory trade measures, citing falling German car sales, and warned that higher costs for steel, aluminium and cement would hit ports and highways. On the India-EU free trade agreement, he said it may be signed by the end of 2026 and be operational within four to five months. Mint reports the deal would give over 99 percent of Indian exports by value preferential access and that the EU would remove tariffs on about 70.4 percent of tariff lines immediately. On the US side, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on 20 October the two countries are about as close as you can be without having executed the trade deal, with a small number of items left; India wants a final US tariff comparable to Vietnam's.

stories.title: Modi and Tusk agree to aim for double the trade by 2030 and open defence-industry and counter-terrorism dialogues
stories.summary: Poland's prime minister, on his first India visit in 16 years as PM, met Modi at Hyderabad House on 22 October. Bilateral trade is about 6 billion dollars; both backed finishing the EU-India trade deal.
stories.heat: Outlook India, digests, MEA readout · Ground News Blindspot: Bengaluru business forum, 6 sources, 17 percent left
detail: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk began a three-day visit to India on 21 October 2026, the first by a Polish prime minister in 16 years, and held talks with Narendra Modi at Hyderabad House in New Delhi on 22 October. The two sides agreed to aim to double bilateral trade, currently about 6 billion dollars, by 2030, and to set up a defence-industry dialogue and a counter-terrorism dialogue. Both backed concluding the EU-India free trade agreement. Business forums are scheduled in New Delhi and Bengaluru. Outlook India reported before the visit that Poland's own target is 10 billion dollars a year. The relationship was upgraded to a strategic partnership during Modi's August 2024 visit to Warsaw; trade was 5.72 billion dollars in 2023, up 192 percent in a decade.

Update for this edition: on the last day of the visit Tusk addressed the India-Poland Business Forum in Bengaluru and called for technological cooperation. Ground News flags the story as a Blindspot: 6 sources, 67 percent of them right-leaning and 17 percent left.

stories.title: RBI minutes: unanimous 25 bps hike to 5.50 percent, 4-2 for calibrated tightening, cuts off the table
stories.summary: External members Nagesh Kumar and Ram Singh wanted to keep a neutral stance. CPI was 5.54 percent in September. The 10-year yield sits near 7.25 percent while the rupee firmed on FX measures and IPO inflows.
stories.heat: Business Standard, FXStreet, DBS note · minutes out 21 October · digested
detail: The minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee's 5 to 7 October meeting, released on 21 October 2026, show all six members voted for the 25 basis point repo rate hike to 5.50 percent. The shift in stance from neutral to calibrated tightening passed 4 to 2, with external members Nagesh Kumar and Ram Singh dissenting; Singh argued inflation is mainly supply-driven. Governor Sanjay Malhotra said rate cuts are off the table in the near term, and the resolution's wording is that the next move can only be a hike or a pause. Headline CPI was 5.54 percent in September, near the top of the 4 percent plus or minus 2 band; September WPI was 11.39 percent.

Bond yields rose after the decision, with the benchmark 10-year around 7.25 percent from 7.19. The rupee moved the other way: DBS's Radhika Rao notes the divergence of higher yields with a firmer currency, which she and others attribute to foreign-exchange regulatory measures, IPO-related inflows and tighter oversight of overseas investment. Also in the week's economic record: merchandise exports rose 23.04 percent to 44.40 billion dollars in September; the RBI set Rs 14,425 per unit as the final redemption price for Sovereign Gold Bond 2018-19 Series II maturing 23 October; and the Supreme Court upheld the Bombay High Court's 2023 reversal of the YES Bank AT1 bond write-off, calling the RBI a mere bystander (two sources, per the digest).

stories.title: The eMudhra exit, seen from India: a Bengaluru-listed CA walks away from a global line of business after a key-generation failure
stories.summary: The company says TLS was about 1 percent of revenue and that its signing, eSign and PKI businesses are untouched. The full account is in the Tech section.
stories.heat: HN 1,068 pts · Business Standard, Analytics India Magazine, Indian Opinion
detail: eMudhra (BSE 543533, NSE EMUDHRA) announced on 22 October 2026 that it is exiting the global SSL/TLS certificate business after eight of its intermediate certificate authorities were found to have guessable private keys and Chrome and Firefox moved to distrust its emSign ECC root. The Indian angle is that this is one of the few Indian companies operating a publicly trusted root, and it chose withdrawal over the remediation Chrome's root programme was asking for. The company stresses that digital signature certificates, eSign and PKI services continue. Business Standard's report on the share-price reaction could not be read this run. See the Tech card for the full timeline.

stories.title: Also: Ladakh hill councils reshaped, three sites on UNESCO's tentative list, SIM binding for messaging apps from January 2027, Delhi HC lets Doosra release
stories.summary: Smaller items from the day's digests, one or two lines each.
stories.heat: UNI digest, FreeJobAlert and Indian Opinion digests, Ground News India · 1 to 9 sources each
detail: The Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council (Amendment) Regulation 2026, promulgated by the President on 16 October and in force from 19 October, extends hill councils to all eight districts with between 7 and 24 seats each. India added three sites to UNESCO's Tentative List on 20 October (the Baratang karst and mud-volcano complex, the Andaman subduction volcanoes and Sirpur), taking the list to 81. The Department of Telecommunications requires SIM binding for WhatsApp, Telegram and Signal from 1 January 2027, with a compliance deadline of 31 December 2026; cyber-fraud losses topped Rs 22,800 crore in 2025. The Delhi High Court on 23 October declined to stay the release of the film Doosra in a personality-rights suit brought by Sourav Ganguly and Luv Films, with the next hearing on Friday. Kalyan Gautam was sworn in as the 19th Governor of Sikkim on Monday amid protests over alleged links to the 2022 Ankita Bhandari case. The Defence Ministry signed a Rs 770 crore contract with BEL on 21 October for improved low-level light-weight radars. The India-New Zealand FTA entered into force on 20 October, India's 17th, with a one-year work scheme for 1,000 young Indians. Bihar's STET moves from 4 to 21 November.

Added in this edition, from UNI's 23 October digest: the Centre extended the duty-free raw sugar import deadline to 31 December; Haryana's power strike continues, with minister Anil Vij saying a solution is almost reached and invoking Section 108 before talks with unions; Sukhpal Khaira, suspended from the Punjab Assembly, said he would keep speaking for Punjab; the NIA is examining an IED angle in a Bengaluru blast; four people died and 23 were injured during a week of Durga Puja celebrations in Tripura; and a magnitude 3.0 earthquake was recorded in Bengaluru Rural district. Ground News also lists a Bombay High Court order flagging fake Aadhaar and voter IDs held by foreign infiltrators and ordering a probe (1 source, unverified), and a Swiggy Q2 result flagged as a Blindspot whose figures (loss of Rs 922 crore, revenue up 36 percent) still could not be matched to any other report.
